content: The cooling fans hummed a low, mechanical dirge that chewed on the silence, vibrating through the raised floorboards like a heartbeat in a morgue. Cold, recycled air cut through the stagnant heat of the server racks, carrying the sharp scent of ozone and overheating silicon that clung to the back of my throat like cheap gin. Row after row of blinking status lights flickered in the gloom—a dense, digital starfield of pulsing blues and arterial reds—casting jagged, unnatural shadows against the caged aisles. Somewhere in the dark, a drive clicked rhythmically, a persistent, stuttering heartbeat signaling that, in this vault of glass and copper, the truth was being shredded into binary dust, and I was just another ghost caught in the loop.
